body:
**The headline measurement, with its scope flattened - and this is the header contract.**

> There is no power-up latch on **gen1 silicon**

The `.c` this line points at scopes it correctly, at `:39-41`:

> **On the one tested while ARMED, an ST LRi2K**: the UID changes IMMEDIATELY -- an inventory in the SAME field session as the write already returns the new one -- so there is no power-up latch on **that chip**

One armed chip, not the family. And the three-chip result at `:38` cannot be doing any work here: "the sequence sets the UID, it reads back, and the original restores byte-identically" all passes *through* a power-cycle, so it is silent on whether a latch exists. Only the same-session inventory on the LRi2K shows immediacy.

`7818909c` wrote both lines. `.c:41` says "that chip", the commit message says "this chip", and `:105` of this same header says "Hardware-validated across three chips ... says what that does and does not cover". This one line is the only place it becomes a property of gen1 silicon.

It matters more here than it would in the `.c` because this is the public API doc. A maintainer meeting a different gen1 chip reads this as settled and drops the power-cycle - and the rest of the sentence is the reason to keep it anyway, so the over-claim buys nothing.

"on the gen1 chip tested" and it matches everything around it. (`:36`'s heading, "WHAT IS MEASURED on gen1 silicon", has the same looseness, but its body is precise so it reads as a topic label - much less load-bearing.)

The poller works this out correctly and the release notes got the lossy version.

> the sweep continues past the advertised count until eight blocks in a row answer nothing, so it touches 56/57 **only from a claim of 49 or more**

`iso15693_poller.c:1303-1308`, same delta:

> Two things stop the sweep short of 56/57, and only two: the card ANSWERS NOTHING **above its claim** AND claims fewer than 49 blocks -- **a card that refuses every write but still serves a read never accumulates a run, so it walks past 56/57 whatever it claims**

and `:1311` even adds "49 is not a threshold about the claim CONTAINING 56."

That carve-out is the whole point and the CHANGELOG drops it. `absent_run` increments only at `:996`, where the write *and* the read both failed, and is reset by `wipe_note_present` (`:838`), never at the claim boundary. So the reach depends on when the card stops answering READS:

| card | last block attempted | needs claim |
|---|---|---|
| answers reads everywhere | 256 ceiling or the 10s clock | **any** - a claim of 20 reaches 56/57 |
| answers to its claim, then silent | N+7 | >= 49 |
| silent throughout | max(7, N-1) | >= 57 |

49 is exactly the middle row, published as the general rule. The top row is the card this feature's time limit exists for and the card that produces `wiped == 0`, so it is the one the bullet is about.

Note the edit also removed the old sentence's correct identification of that card ("on the card it can actually happen to - one that answers reads at every address"), so this went from right-with-a-wrong-number to wrong-in-kind.

Third round running for this sentence - unconditional in r8, the `<57` exception in r9, this now. I would stop giving a number and say the reach depends on when the card stops answering reads, naming the read-everywhere card as the dangerous case. The poller's wording is already that; the CHANGELOG can just follow it.

`1cb693de`'s message ends:

> A note at the branch says why there is no validation line, so a later pass does not add one back.

There is no such note. This scene has 18 comment lines and none mentions validation, testing or hardware - `grep -niE "valid|test|hardware"` over the file returns nothing.

The removals themselves are right, and I checked the consent text still carries all three things it owes a user before a destructive write: what gen1 writes, which four blocks, and what is lost on a tag that turns out not to be gen1. Nothing else on the screen or in the CHANGELOG overstates the safety.

But the guard the message describes is the whole reason a later pass would not quietly restore a validation claim to a **consent screen**, and it does not exist. Either write it or drop the sentence from the message - right now the commit log asserts a protection the tree does not have.

Dead conjunct, and the comment above it explains why.

```c
return instance->iso15693_mode == NfcMagicIso15693ModeWipe && !result->uid_verified;
```

`uid_verified` is set true at exactly one place, `iso15693_poller.c:1466`, inside `Iso15693WriteStateVerifyWipe` - and that state's only exit is `success_or_partial`, never CardLost. So a CardLost result always has `uid_verified == false` and the second term cannot be false here.

`:66-67` says it itself: "the run returns before Iso15693WriteStateVerifyWipe is entered".

Harmless as belt-and-braces, and I would not raise it except that `d431fea9`'s message justifies the term with "a wipe that lost the card after the check answered has nothing left to report" - a state the poller cannot produce. Same class as the `mode != Info` conjunct from round 7. Either drop the term or keep it and say it is defensive rather than load-bearing.

Four mangled comment wraps, bundled - all pre-existing, none from this round, and `ReflowComments: false` means `ufbt format` cannot see any of them. Flagging as a set since the rewrap pass in `5bc041d4` reached some and missed these.

- **here, `:59`** (17 cols) - "// written out at" / "// its call site, where the order is the point." [`297b5ca9`]
- `iso15693_poller.h:44` (56 cols) - "... Which of those it was is" / "// in Iso15693PollerResult ..." [`de233993`]
- `nfc_magic_scene_iso15693_partial_details.c:88` (42 cols) - "// under-reports (the trailing run" / "// the tail-drop discards ..." [`0bee8cb6`]
- `magic/protocols/iso15693/iso15693_info.c:261` (27 cols) - "// decodes the same bits in" / "// slix.c (...)" [`acc486b1`]

Each is a paragraph that lost its reflow when text above it was edited. Purely cosmetic.

Small one, pre-existing: this comment says

> ISO15693 **clone** treats card-lost as terminal

but the branch it sits on fires for a wipe and a Write-UID too - `Iso15693PollerEventCardLost` reaches here from `iso15693_poller.c:1293` (wipe) and from the gen1/gen2 verifies, not only the clone.

Nothing acts on it, and everything the branch does is right for all three modes. Just drop "clone" - the reasoning underneath is mode-independent.
